page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c6r.xlarge is a compute-optimized instance provisioned on the KVM hypervisor. It features 4 dedicated arm64 vCPUs powered by an Ampere Altra processor operating at 2.8 GHz, paired with 8.0 GB of system memory, yielding a 2.0 GB per vCPU ratio. The instance does not include local disk storage or discrete GPUs, relying on attached block storage, and provides a baseline network bandwidth of 1 Gbps with no complimentary public IPv4 addresses. Hardware capabilities include ARM AES encryption instructions, while x86-specific vector and matrix extensions are absent.

Benchmark evaluations highlight mixed performance characteristics across different operational profiles. The instance demonstrates average performance in stress-ng single-core and multi-core CPU tests, as well as large-block uncached memory read and write bandwidth. PassMark database operations and text generation throughput for small 135M parameter LLM models also perform in the middle benchmark tier. In contrast, single-threaded workloads including Geekbench processing, gzip compression, bzip3 decompression, and Redis SET throughput fall into lower performance brackets, with PassMark CPU encryption ranking in the lowest percentile tier.

The instance delivers dedicated ARM processing resources suitable for cost-aware deployment of scaling microservices and ARM-native pipelines. Due to the absence of bundled local storage and modest single-core throughput, Alibaba Cloud ecs.c6r.xlarge is best deployed for containerized workloads, ARM build servers, light web application tiers, and basic database operations.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c6r.xlarge is a compute-optimized server instance running on a KVM hypervisor. Powered by a 4-vCPU dedicated Ampere Altra arm64 processor clocked at 2.8 GHz, it is equipped with 8.0 GB of RAM, offering a 2.0 GB per vCPU allocation ratio. The server lacks local storage and discrete GPUs, operating with a 1 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. Benchmark results demonstrate average multi-core CPU throughput in stress-ng testing, standard uncached memory bandwidth, and average PassMark database operation rates. Conversely, single-core processing tasks, including Geekbench benchmarks, compression workloads, and PassMark encryption tests, yield lower performance scores. This instance provides uniform ARM execution suited for containerized microservices, ARM native software development, micro-benchmarks, and standard database tasks.
